title: Unit Circle Definition
text: $$\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$$ represents the $$x-$$ coordinate of the point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{-\pi}{3}.$$\n##figure1.gif##

title: Reference Angle
text: The reference angle for $$-\frac{\pi}{3}$$ is $$\frac{\pi}{3}.$$ The absolute values of the coordinates are given by the legs of a $$30-60-90$$ triangle with hypotenuse $$1$$. The x-coordinate length comes from the side adjacent to the 60-degree angle, which is $$\frac{1}{2}.$$\n##figure2.gif##

title: Quadrant Sign
text: The angle $$-\frac{\pi}{3}$$ is in the fourth quadrant, where $$x-$$ coordinates are positive. Therefore, $$\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{1}{2}.$$\n##figure3.gif##
